bib.title: From Skills to Talent: Organising Heterogeneous Agents as a Real-World Company

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "From Skills to Talent: Organising Heterogeneous Agents as a Real-World Company" (OneManCompany, OMC). Zhengxu Yu, Yu Fu (co-first), Zhiyuan He, Yuxuan Huang, Lee Ka Yiu, Meng Fang, Weilin Luo, Jun Wang. Huawei Noah's Ark Lab, UCL, Univ. Liverpool. arXiv:2604.22446v1 [cs.AI], 24 Apr 2026. Preprint, not peer reviewed (no venue printed).

COVERAGE: all 104,253 chars of extraction read (main text, related work, limitations, appendices A-H). References only skimmed for origins. Figure pixels not viewed; only captions/text. Run was cwd-local, extraction saved at /tmp/yu.txt.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- OMC reaches 84.67% success on PRDBench, 15.48 points above the best baseline.
  number: 84.67% (+15.48); cost $345.59 over 50 tasks (~$6.91/task)
  setup: PRDBench, 50 project-level tasks across 20+ domains, official DEV mode (one-shot PRD, no feedback), success rate metric. Team: LangGraph founding agent on Gemini Flash Lite Preview, plus HR-recruited Claude Code Software Engineer (superpowers plugin), Software Architect and Code Reviewer (agency-agents). Table 2 labels the system "Claude Code Sonnet 4.6 + Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Preview"; the setup text says "Gemini 2.1 Flash Lite Preview" (inconsistent).
  quote: "OMC achieves the highest success rate of 84.67% (+15.48%) across all systems, surpassing all baselines. The total cost of $345.59 across 50 tasks (approximately $6.91 per task)"
  where: Sec 3.2, Table 2, p13-14
- Baselines in the same table: best single model Claude-4.5 minimal 69.19, GPT-5.2 62.49, CodeX 62.09, Claude Code 56.65, Gemini CLI 11.29.
  quote: "Minimal Claude-4.5 69.19" / "Commercial Claude Code 56.65" (Table 2)
  where: p14. These are numbers copied from PRDBench, not rerun. Baseline cost was not reported, so there is no cost comparison.
- Topology: a hierarchical manager tree with DAG dependencies. The CEO creates the root. A supervisor (COO or senior employee) acts as the policy that "jointly decides decomposition granularity and employee assignment". Interior nodes are sub-tasks and leaves are atomic tasks assigned to single employees. Decomposition edges form a strict tree; dependency edges may cross sibling branches; the union must be a DAG, enforced by DFS cycle detection at insertion.
  number: none
  quote: "The combined graph 𝐺=(𝑉,𝐸 tree∪𝐸 dep)must be a DAG, enforced at insertion time via DFS cycle detection." and "The supervisor serves as the heuristic policy that jointly decides decomposition granularity and employee assignment."
  where: Sec 2.2.1, p8
- Role assignment is a tree action. Five action types: decompose, assign, recruit, review, iterate. Recruit fires when the workforce lacks a capability (HR queries the Talent Market, ranks a shortlist, and the human CEO approves). Explore stage frames assignment as exploitation (proven employees) vs exploration (untested or new hire).
  quote: "A=A decompose∪A assign∪A recruit∪A review∪A iterate"
  where: Eq. 2, p8
- Review-gated AND-semantics. A node is resolved only if all children are resolved, so no subtask is silently dropped. A completed→accepted transition needs explicit supervisor review before dependents unblock. Reject triggers re-decomposition under the same parent.
  quote: "completed→acceptedrequires explicit supervisor review, which prevents hallucinated or incorrect results from unblocking dependent tasks."
  where: Sec 2.2.4, p11; Eq. 10
- Termination and deadlock safeguards, with seven invariants (DAG, mutual exclusion |running(e)|≤1, schedule idempotency, review termination, cascade completeness, dependency completeness, crash recovery). Defaults: review-round limit k_rev=3 then escalate, task timeout 3600 s, a cost budget that pauses. A deadlock detector marks the project failed if all non-root nodes are terminal or blocked but the root is unresolved. The "formal guarantees" are design arguments, with no mechanised proof shown, and they hold only if the executor respects the timeout contract.
  quote: "(𝑛rev(𝑣)≥𝑘 rev =⇒esc(𝑣),default𝑘 rev=3),atasktimeout(𝑡 exec(𝑣)>𝑇 max =⇒𝜙 𝑣←failed,default 𝑇max =3600s)"
  where: Sec 2.2.3, p10
- E2R is MCTS-inspired only structurally: no rollouts, no UCB, review is an explicit supervisor accept/reject, and the policy is the LLM supervisor with context enriched across iterations, not learned.
  quote: "UnlikeMCTS,E 2RdoesnotusesimulatedrolloutsorUCB-basedselection"
  where: Sec 2.2, p7
- Human CEO is an external oracle (policy override, requirement injection, iteration trigger). Convergence depends on human judgment, not formal guarantees.
  quote: "The trade-off is that convergence depends on the quality of human judgment rather than on formal guarantees."
  where: Sec 2.2.2, p10
- Talent/Container split: a portable agent identity (role, prompts, skills, tools, principles) is separate from the runtime (LangGraph, Claude Code, script) behind six typed interfaces (Execution, Task, Event, Storage, Context, Lifecycle), mapped to OS kernel subsystems (App. B). Founding team: HR, EA, COO, CSO.
  where: Sec 2.1, p5-6, App A-B
- HR lifecycle: a review every three projects; three consecutive failures lead to a performance improvement plan (PIP); one more failure under PIP leads to offboarding and re-recruitment. Self-evolution edits Talent artefacts (principles, SOPs), not model weights. Not ablated.
  where: Sec 2.3, p12-13
- Case studies (qualitative, single runs): GitHub trend report under 10 min, ~$4.48 (Researcher GPT-4o, Writer Claude Sonnet 4); audiobook $1.57 (~1.56M tokens, 15.7% of a $10 budget); research survey $16.26 across 15.9M tokens; game development shows human-evaluator rejection leading to a new skill and re-execution.
  quote: "$1.57 for 16 scenes, 16 voice-over tracks, background music, and two final videos"
  where: Sec 3.3, App F-H
- Related-work claim relayed from others: heterogeneous DAG topologies beat homogeneous ones (X-MAS, MacNet); compact core teams work best. Not tested here.
  quote: "X-MAS [19] and MacNet [20] show that heterogeneous DAG topologies outperform homogeneous baselines"
  where: Sec 4, p18

LIMITS
- Authors concede: quantitative evaluation is only PRDBench (50 coding tasks); no non-coding benchmark. Self-evolution mechanisms are "not yet quantitatively ablated". Cost is high (~$6.91/task). They list as open: whether the advantage holds at larger scale and each component's isolated contribution.
- Not shown (my reading): no ablation of the tree, the review gate or the heterogeneous team, so the three "contributing aspects" in Sec 3.2 are asserted, not measured. There is no single-agent control using the same Claude Code Sonnet 4.6 backend. The baselines are copied, not rerun, and their cost is unknown, so the gain may partly come from spending more. One run per task, no variance or seeds reported. No topology comparison (flat vs hierarchical vs mesh). The recruitment shortlist is human-approved, so "self-organising" is semi-supervised. Formal guarantees are not proved in a checkable sense. The Related Work states "none provides formal guarantees" without testing competitors. Authors' own project, with promotional framing ("real-world company"). Model names (Claude-4.5, Gemini-3.1) will date quickly.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
- MCTS: Kocsis and Szepesvari, "Bandit based Monte-Carlo planning", ECML 2006.
- Bounded rationality / meta-level control: Russell and Wefald, Do the Right Thing, MIT Press 1991.
- Dynamic decomposition: TDAG (Wang et al., Neural Networks 2025); Plan-and-Act (Erdogan et al., arXiv 2503.09572, 2025); Hu, Cai et al., "Self-evolving multi-agent collaboration networks for software development", ICLR 2025.
- Heterogeneous/scaled MAS: Magentic-One (Fourney et al., arXiv 2411.04468, 2024); X-MAS (Ye et al., arXiv 2505.16997, 2025); MacNet, "Scaling LLM-based multi-agent collaboration" (Qian et al., ICLR 2025).
- Benchmark: PRDBench (Fu et al., arXiv 2510.24358, 2025). Compared against MetaGPT/ChatDev, AutoGen/LangGraph, CrewAI, OpenHands, AIOS, AgentScope, Paperclip (Table 4).
- OS-kernel analogy: Tanenbaum-style references [13,14].

CODE: none beyond Algorithm 1 (Talent Assembly pseudocode, p7): queue check, AssembleContext(role, principles, guidance, memory), PreHook, V_e.Execute, PostHook, Publish event. Only worth keeping as pseudocode.

FIGURES
- Figure 4 (p9): "An illustration of the E2R tree search loop: Explore, Execute, Review." Shows root, interior and leaf nodes, with dependency edges. Best candidate for the topology note. Figure 5 (p11, task lifecycle FSM) is the alternative for the review gate. I did not view the images.

PROBLEMS
- Extraction has no spaces in many words (PDF kerning), but the quotes are verbatim from it. Figure content and Table 4 are partly garbled. Eq. 11 lists "blocked" in the state set, but the terminal set F is given only as {finished, cancelled}. Model name inconsistency noted above (Gemini "2.1" vs "3.1" Flash Lite). The text says 18 deliverables in the Fig. 12 caption while the figure label says 17. The case-study references say "Section 3.3.1" for the survey, which is actually 3.3.4. No embedded instructions found in the PDF.
